author: Antigravity Remote Sensing & Scientific Validation Engine
core_question: Are the harmonised data more comparable than the raw MODIS and VIIRS data?
core_finding: YES for the genuine sensor overlap era (2012–2026) and typical fire regimes (M <= 5), where harmonisation reduces the artificial Jan 2012 seam jump from +1,373.9% to +25.0% and maintains high seasonal correlation (r = 0.933) and peak-month preservation. HOWEVER, Gate B is awarded as a CONDITIONAL PASS because three structural limitations failed: (1) The pre-2002 Terra-only era lacks a diurnal bridge; (2) Extreme forest cell-weeks (M > 10) trigger unconstrained power-law extrapolation; (3) Active-fire uncertainty intervals achieve only 54.64% empirical coverage at nominal 80%.

authorized_for_release: Post-2012 overlap harmonised counts and FRP (weekly and monthly)
2002–2011 dual-MODIS typical fire weeks (with prediction tag)
restricted_or_flagged: Forest cell-weeks with M > 10 (labelled EXTRAPOLATION OUTLIER)
Active-fire uncertainty intervals (must display undercoverage warning)
Daily estimates (must display disaggregated weekly estimate tag)
